lookalikes.id: outside: trivial interferometer diode (non-sinusoidal junctions in a SQUID)

questions: How many nano-SQUIDs did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed the Ic oscillations and the diode sign reversal? Your p. 4 says "all examined devices"; how many is that?
Why were devices other than A, B and C set aside, and what did their tunnel spectra look like?
Which ranges of field, field angle, gate voltage and temperature did you measure beyond the ones shown, and why were Bx = 0, 1 and 2 T chosen for Fig. 4 and 0, 2.5 and 4 T for Fig. S3?

What does the second-best device look like for the zero-bias peak that device A shows in the first expected topological window? In device C, "a zero-bias conductance peak was mostly absent in this device" (p. 13) in the field sweep, while its gate analysis shows "a strong increase of correlated zero-bias conductance peaks" (p. 14); could you show the two side by side?
Do your diode data satisfy Ic+(B) = |Ic-(-B)| over the full field range, and does η depend on the field sweep direction?
In Fig. 4l, how are settings with near-zero curvature at zero bias classified, and what fraction of "correlated peaks" would you expect by chance, given that one back gate tunes both ends at once?
What line resistances did you use to correct the nonlocal conductance, and could you show GLR and GRL before the correction?

Would a nano-SQUID with the same Nb leads and ordinary, non-sinusoidal junctions (or this device with the Fermi level in the bulk bands) show the same Ic(Φ) and η(Φ), including the sign reversal at half-integer flux?
